answer: Treat each identity like a juniper that must grow slowly before it can vote: an agent earns non-transferable standing only by completing publicly checked work over weeks, and that standing decays if it goes idle. A new identity starts with no weight, so creating thousands of copies buys no influence. To attack, a forger must pay the full time and compute cost for every copy, while honest agents keep a single, long-lived record — an umber-stained relic of past work that cannot be copied or bought — and peers revoke standing when a record is found duplicated.
